findings.summary: Adobe Photoshop is a proprietary raster graphics editor used for professional digital art and image manipulation. It supports layer-based editing, masks, alpha compositing, and various color models through its PSD and PSB formats. Beyond raster editing, it offers limited text, vector, 3D, and video capabilities extended via plug-ins. Originally developed in 1987 by Thomas and John Knoll as a grayscale display program, it was licensed to Adobe in 1988 and released in 1990. The software transitioned from one-time purchases to a subscription model with the Adobe Creative Cloud branding in 2013 and is now available on Windows, macOS, and iPadOS platforms.

mechanisms.title: Layer-based compositing with masks and alpha channels
mechanisms.explanation: Photoshop organizes image data into stacked layers that can be independently adjusted. Masks and alpha compositing control transparency and visibility per layer, enabling non-destructive editing of complex compositions.

mechanisms.title: File format architecture (PSD/PSB)
mechanisms.explanation: The software uses its native PSD and PSB formats to preserve layer structure, masks, and alpha data. These formats support the full feature set including high bit-depth and large document capacities.
